plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A leafless-flowering bulb that sends up goblet-shaped pink-lilac blooms directly from the soil in early autumn, while its leaves appear the following spring. Found in damp meadows and widely grown in gardens.
plants.location: Europe, from the UK to the Balkans; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a true crocus. It contains colchicine, a toxic alkaloid that is used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to double chromosome numbers.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower with arching plumes of tiny golden-yellow flower heads. It dominates meadows, roadsides and prairie edges in late summer and autumn and is an important late-season nectar source for pollinators.
plants.location: North America, widely naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but its pollen is heavy and insect-carried; the real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time.

plants.name: Aster novae-angliae
plants.description: A robust native perennial of North American prairies and meadows, topped with masses of daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. It is a crucial late-season food source for migrating monarch butterflies and native bees.
plants.location: Eastern and central North America; popular in cultivation
plants.funFact: The flower heads close up on cloudy days and at night, opening again in full sun.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with umbels of sparkling, narrow-petaled pink flowers with wavy edges that appear on bare stems. It is grown in warm, sunny borders and is native to rocky mountain slopes.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early autumn in the Northern Hemisphere (September-November); native-range flowering in autumn too
plants.location: Native to the Drakensberg mountains of South Africa; grown in the UK, Europe and elsewhere
plants.funFact: The petals have a crystalline sheen that glitters in sunlight, which gives the genus the common nickname 'diamond lily' for some species.
